summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with epistaxis and a supratherapeutic INR of 9.8, likely due to his warfarin therapy despite no recent medication or dietary changes. He had ongoing oozing and blood in his throat after initial management at an outside hospital with a nasal balloon catheter. He was given oral vitamin K and admitted for monitoring. ENT performed cauterization of a bleeding septal vessel with silver nitrate and Surgicell, achieving hemostasis. Warfarin was held during admission and restarted on discharge when his INR reached 2.8. Plavix was held for five days for safety and was to be resumed post-discharge. His baby aspirin was continued throughout due to his history of strokes. He remained stable, with no further bleeding, and was discharged home with visiting nurse INR monitoring and clear follow-up instructions.
